Client meeting brief agent: a walkthrough¶

This notebook walks through the pipeline behind the interactive page, one module at a time. There is no logic in here; every cell imports a module from client_brief_agent/ and calls it, so what you see is exactly what python main.py does. It reads the cached snapshots and models from the last full run.

Client profiles and product holdings are real public data (Kaggle Santander Product Recommendation). KYC review dates, risk profiles and vulnerability flags are synthetic, made up for this prototype.

In [1]:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "..")  # the notebook lives in notebooks/, the package one level up

import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Image, Markdown, display

from client_brief_agent import config
from client_brief_agent.features import build
from client_brief_agent.data import synthetic
from client_brief_agent.models import segment, propensity, explain
from client_brief_agent.agent import tools, run
from client_brief_agent.report import export

pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)
pd.set_option("display.width", 160)

1. The snapshots¶

For a target month T, every feature comes from history up to T minus 1 and the label is "took the product up in T". Training stacks the target months up to March 2016, validation is April, test is May. The brief looks ahead to June 2016, which the data does not contain, so it has no labels.

2. The synthetic layer¶

No public dataset has review dates or risk profiles, so I draw them with a fixed seed, independently of the real data. Nothing in the models reads these fields; only the guardrail and the brief do.

3. Grouping clients¶

k means for k from 2 to 10 on standardised features, chosen by silhouette with the elbow as a tie breaker, then a Gaussian mixture with the same k to see whether a different method finds the same groups.

5. What a score leans on¶

SHAP contributions for LightGBM, turned into short phrases with the client's own recorded values. They describe what moved the score, not why a client would want the product.

In [12]:
display(Image(str(config.FIG_DIR / "shap_global.png"), width=760))

6. The agent¶

The agent is a fixed sequence of small tool calls, each one logged: profile, segment, recent changes, propensities, a suitability check per product, a linked products check, the review date and the questions. Here is the brief for the first showcase client. The page shows clients by a reference only, so I do the same here.

In [13]:
brief = frames["brief"]
ctx = tools.Context(snapshot=brief, segments=seg, scores=propensity.score(models, brief),
                    reasons=explain.reasons_provider(models, brief), synthetic=layer, bands=bands)
picks = export.choose_showcase(ctx)
first_id, picked_for = picks[0]
example = run.run_brief(ctx, first_id, ref="Client 01")
print("picked because:", ", ".join(picked_for))
display(Markdown(run.render_markdown(example)))

picked because: cluster 0 example, recent change new_client, recent change segment_change

Meeting brief: Client 01¶

Meeting on 1 June 2016. Prepared to support the conversation. Scores are estimates, not instructions; the advisor decides what to discuss.

1. Who this client is¶

Younger students (cluster 0): Mostly students (99%), younger (average age 24), newer clients (about 3 years with the bank).

Aged 19, joined this month, income not recorded, holds no products.

Recent changes:

  • Joined the bank in the last six months (this month).
  • Client segment changed in the last six months.

2. What might help¶

  • Current account, scores above 50%. In the test month, 44% of the 456 clients scoring between 50% and 100% took it up. The score leans on: joined this month; aged 19; changed customer segment in the last six months.

3. What not to offer¶

No high scoring product was held back by the suitability check.

4. Due anyway¶

No periodic review is due within 90 days; the next one is on 29 April 2018.

Review dates come from a synthetic layer made for this prototype, not real records.

5. Questions to open with¶

  1. How have your first months with us gone, and is there anything you expected that is not set up yet?
  2. Your situation with us has changed a little recently. Are your current accounts still a good fit for how you live now?
  3. What are your thoughts on your everyday money at the moment?

How this brief was prepared¶

  1. get_profile: aged 19, no products held
  2. get_segment: cluster 0, Younger students
  3. get_recent_changes: 2 change flags
  4. get_propensities: 8 products scored, highest Current account (above 50%)
  5. check_suitability: Current account: allowed
  6. check_review_due: not due, next review 2018-04-29 (697 days)
  7. draft_questions: 3 questions drafted

7. The guardrail across every client¶

The same rules, vectorised over all clients, for a range of thresholds. A high score never overrides fit.
